summary: Inject control-flow heuristic to distrust negative VQA consensus after tool failure, using generic terminology to avoid leakage.

edits.hypothesis: Adding a control-flow injection that triggers when a targeted inspection tool fails prevents the agent from uncritically accepting negative consensus from general VQA models, addressing the 'uncritical_acceptance_of_contradictory_vqa_output' failure mode.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt edits in AGENT_SYSTEM are static and may be diluted by long context; a control-flow injection ensures the directive is active precisely when the failure condition (tool crash) occurs, providing immediate contextual reinforcement.
edits.trigger_condition: Any tool call in the current step returns a failure status detected by tool_failure_reason.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000001, roi_crop failed. The new message would have warned against accepting llava_med_qa's negative output, prompting re-examination of the original image. (preservative) In q000006, where roi_crop also failed but the agent correctly triangulated with other tools, the warning serves as a reminder but does not disrupt the successful multi-tool strategy. (transfer) Generalizes to any domain where high-resolution or specialized tools fail and fallback models provide low-confidence negatives.
edits.regression_risk: Minimal. The message is generic and only activates on failure. It might cause slight hesitation if the agent was already confident, but accuracy gain from correcting false negatives outweighs this.
edits.mechanism: Adding a control-flow injection that triggers when a targeted inspection tool fails prevents the agent from uncritically accepting negative consensus from general VQA models, addressing the 'uncritical_acceptance_of_contradictory_vqa_output' failure mode.
